- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.50), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect market resilience.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +5–10% in 1–2 days); apply smoothing or lagged decay to prevent overshoot.
- In 30-day horizon, model frequently fails to capture mean reversion after strong upward moves; add downward bias after peak price days.
- If sentiment turns negative after a peak, model often fails to anticipate sharp drop; apply early warning correction (e.g., -2–3% below forecast).
- Model underestimates when sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.00–0.33); increase forecast by 1–2% to account for latent market momentum.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to be too optimistic in early days (e.g., first 5–7 days); apply downward bias of 1–3% for first 7 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
